html:
Juan José Arévalo was a Guatemalan teacher and philosopher who became the first democratically elected president of Guatemala, ruling from 1945 to 1951. His term opened the Ten Years of Spring.

In 1944 students, teachers and young officers overthrew the dictator Jorge Ubico in the October Revolution. Arévalo, who had lived in exile in Argentina, came home and won a landslide. He called his ideas spiritual socialism.

He brought in a new constitution, a labour code, social security, and a large literacy campaign, and gave workers the right to organise. He survived many coup attempts. In 1951 he handed power to the elected Jacobo Árbenz, whose land reform led to the coup of 1954. The Spring is remembered in Guatemala as a lost chance.
sum: Juan José Arévalo was a Guatemalan teacher and philosopher who became the first democratically elected president of Guatemala, ruling from 1945 to 1951. His term opened the Ten Years of Spring.
